solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: What chef prepares food on duty? The best!

parts.note: a duty is one's work or task
the best is the top, as in 'top of the class'

explanation.surface: A question about a chef's duty, answered with an exclamation of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen counter surface is where a cook chops and assembles ingredients.

clue.text: Women are dancing the twist

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ladies are doing an old dance called the twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' at the end looks like the 1960s dance continuing the surface, but it is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreathe is to twist or entwine, as of strands around something.

clue.text: Extra something inaccurate tennis player might do?

definitions.meaning: a spare held in hand, kept back for later

definitions.text: something inaccurate tennis player might do?
definitions.meaning: a player who misses the first serve gets to serve again

explanation.definitionFit: A reserve is an extra kept in hand; read as re-serve it means serving once more.

clue.text: Dance beat with energy

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A dance with an energetic rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance originating in Argentina.

clue.text: Sheer drop in cost is epic, possibly

indicators.note: the rearranged word is set inside the word for cost

parts.note: price means cost

indicators.note: possibly says the word may be in another arrangement

explanation.surface: A steep fall in price is said to be epic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is only a link word; 'possibly' rearranges 'epic' before it goes in the cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliff face with a sheer vertical drop is a steep, dangerous edge.

clue.text: Travelled on horse, by the sound of it, with Member of Parliament holding a route finder?

indicators.note: tells us the word for riding on horseback is to be replaced by one spoken the same way

parts.note: rode is the past tense of ride, travelling on horseback

indicators.note: the politician's abbreviation holds the next small word inside it

explanation.surface: A rider and an MP set out together carrying a guide to the route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' means the politician's letters hold the article 'a', and the question mark admits that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A road atlas sheet is literally something used to find a route; the question mark flags the playful phrasing.

clue.text: Gran cooked on English stove

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored into a new form

explanation.surface: Grandma prepared a meal on an English cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a range is an old-fashioned kitchen cooker, such as an Aga; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large kitchen stove with several hobs and ovens.

clue.text: Those who criticise fancy cakes and tart

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters are dressed up anew

explanation.surface: Critics of ornate patisserie and a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like the cakes' description but signals rearranging CAKES and TART.
explanation.definitionFit: People who attack something verbally are its critics or detractors.

clue.text: Swallow one drink

parts.note: the martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Gulp down a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth.

clue.text: People regularly want fish

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

parts.note: want means lack, as in 'for want of'

explanation.surface: People often want to eat fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of PEOPLE: P, O, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollack is a food fish of the cod family found in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Ascetic possessing cold nature

indicators.note: the ascetic holds the abbreviation for cold within himself

parts.note: the Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the Second Temple period
C is the usual abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A self-denying hermit who has a chilly temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: The basic character or intrinsic quality of a thing is its essential being.

clue.text: Typical ancient city in old African province

indicators.note: the ancient city is placed inside the province's name

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa until 1994
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A characteristic ancient city located in a former African region.
explanation.definitionFit: Something typical is normal or usual, true to its innate character.

clue.text: Bully's mistake — wearing crooked ties

indicators.note: the jumbled ties are worn around the mistake, so they enclose it
crooked suggests the ties are askew, so their letters are bent out of order

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A bully's fashion blunder: wearing ties that hang askew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' looks like it belongs with the ties, but it tells the rearranged ties to go round the mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them, filling them with fear.

clue.text: Strike a mate

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the chin

explanation.surface: An instruction to hit a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate', so a china is a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: a china, from china plate, is a friend or pal.

clue.text: Conclusion about this compiler's correct

indicators.note: the conclusion goes round, or about, the compiler's pronoun

parts.note: an end is a conclusion
the setter refers to himself, giving me

explanation.surface: The setter claims his own ending is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct or improve it by editing.

clue.text: Party held to annoy American? Risky

indicators.note: the party holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a do is a party
to anger is to annoy
US is short for American, as in US citizen

explanation.surface: A party organised to irritate an American is hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risky is perilous or hazardous.

clue.text: Spinning, thin pike caught not initially in perfect condition

indicators.note: the spun letters catch the next piece and hold it inside
a spinning fish is twisting, so the letters whirl into a new order
initially points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An angler watches a skinny pike thrashing on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' rearranges THIN PIKE into ITHEPINK, and N (first of 'not') is caught after its I.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being in fine health or excellent shape is described with this pink phrase.

clue.text: Bird's poorly — took food to stimulate

parts.note: a tit is a small bird; the 's is no letter
poorly means ill
ate means took food

explanation.surface: A sick bird ate something to perk itself up.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to excite or arouse pleasurably.

clue.text: Needing support of French writer, having depression

parts.note: de is French for of
a pen is a writing instrument
a dent is a hollow or depression

explanation.surface: A French author who suffers from low spirits and relies on others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reliant on others for help or upkeep is unable to stand alone.

clue.text: Colour scheme by mummy oddly ignored good taste

parts.note: decor is the furnishing and colour scheme of a room

indicators.note: oddly ignored means skipping the odd-numbered letters and keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Mum ignored the colour scheme, showing poor taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' drops M, M, Y from MUMMY, leaving U and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is propriety and good taste in behaviour.

clue.text: Left on ship with one working part

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral one
on means working, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A sailor stays on board with one job to do.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a part or share of something.

clue.text: Some task I'm prepared to economise

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers for a job that will save money.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to spend as little as possible, cutting corners to save money.

clue.text: Bogarde, perhaps, missing first part? Tedious

indicators.note: missing first means the actor's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Dirk Bogarde was a British film actor, so he exemplifies the name Dirk
some means a part of something

explanation.surface: Was the actor Bogarde missing his opening part?
explanation.walkthrough: Dirk Bogarde was a British film star of the 1950s-70s; DIRK less D gives IRK.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irksome is annoying and wearisome, so tedious.

clue.text: Don crept out, ignoring BBC's last forecast

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of place and rearranged
last points to the final letter of the broadcaster's name

explanation.surface: A man named Don sneaked out, ignoring the BBC weather forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: DON CREPT, 'ignoring' C (the last letter of 'BBC's'), leaves DONREPT, which 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow or foretell a future event.

clue.text: Plague remedy includes sulphur

indicators.note: the remedy takes in the element symbol, holding it inside

parts.note: a cure is a remedy
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A treatment for the plague contains sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague or affliction is a scourge visited upon someone, like a hex.

clue.text: All at sea like tar — on this?

definitions.text: All at sea like tar — on this?

indicators.note: being all at sea means in confusion, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A confused sailor wonders what vessel he is aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All at sea' scrambles LIKE TAR ON; the whole clue also describes a vessel carrying black, tarry crude across the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship for carrying crude petroleum sails the seas loaded with tarry black cargo.

clue.text: Genesis on television

parts.note: a set is a television set

explanation.surface: The Bible's opening book broadcast on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means beginning or origin, the start of something.

clue.text: Copying recording but missing start

indicators.note: missing start means the word for recording loses its first letter

parts.note: taping means recording

explanation.surface: Duplicating a recording that lacks its opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Aping means imitating or mimicking, as monkeys are thought to do.

clue.text: Rock tour in US without hit, finally getting wrecked

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters are jolted into a new order
finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A rock band's American tour ends in disaster after no hit records.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUR IN US, 'without' T (the last letter of 'hit'), leaves OURINUS, which 'Rock' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in ruins is destroyed or devastated, like a wrecked building.

clue.text: Fatty apes do start to ignore bananas

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild
start to points to the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Overweight apes begin to ignore their bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' scrambles APES DO plus I, the first letter of 'ignore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is body fat; the word is a technical term for fat-storing.

clue.text: Beware of group's fixed attitude

parts.note: mind the gap means beware of the gap
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A warning about a clique's rigid views.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual way of thinking that resists change is a fixed mental attitude.

clue.text: Intellectual urge by school principal

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
the head is the headteacher of a school

explanation.surface: A clever headteacher urges pupils on.
explanation.definitionFit: A highbrow or bookish person is informally called by this word.
